A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, equations, Table 1, Figures 1–9, and Appendices A–B are readable and support comparison despite renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original model-fitting experiments and accuracy comparisons using two human kidney-allocation datasets and five simulated decision-makers, including participant-level and training-size analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and Appendix B. Reusing previously collected human data does not change the originality of the reported modeling experiments.

M1.justification: The contextual feature-editing and aggregation framework, monotonicity constraints, regularization, and cross-entropy/hinge variants remain unchanged. The added conditional GAM-tree characterization does not introduce a different training or inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same kidney-allocation studies with 15 and 40 participants and the same five synthetic decision-makers, DM1–DM5. Patient features, simulated heuristics, and task coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Drift-Diffusion, Bradley-Terry, and the same eight supervised baselines. Comparator membership also matches within the case studies, participant-level comparisons, and training-size analysis.

E3.justification: Both versions retain random 70/30 train/test splits, the 20% training-data validation holdout for context selection, accuracy evaluation, dataset filtering, and the training-size sweep from 10 to 100. Appendix B documents the same experimental settings.

E4.justification: The P4 and DM1 case studies, DM2–DM5 heuristic-recovery results, individual-participant comparisons, and training-size sensitivity analysis all already appear in v1 and are retained in v2.

E5.justification: Both versions report 20 repetitions, average accuracies with standard deviations, and the same graphical variability displays. No repeated-run, uncertainty-estimation, or significance-testing practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: Table 1 values, case-study accuracies, and plotted empirical results match. For example, cross-entropy model accuracies remain .90, .90, and .89 across the three dataset columns. Figures 2–9 retain the same results despite relocation.

T1.justification: V2 moves continuity into the weak-transitivity axiom and explicitly adds complementarity to Theorem 3.4's assumptions, correcting its omission from v1's corresponding statement despite its use in the proof. Theorem 3.6 adds a conditional GAM-tree characterization; Appendix A otherwise retains the proofs and does not explicitly prove the added item.

C1.justification: The central cognitive-fidelity, interpretability, and predictive-accuracy claims remain. V2's introduction adds an explicit claim that its axioms are substantially weaker than classical choice axioms and accommodate empirically observed heuristic processes without those classical restrictions.

C2.justification: V2 expands the descriptive-versus-prescriptive interpretation of the axioms and explicitly questions alignment to actual versus idealized human reasoning. It removes the proposed correction of undesirable heuristics, the hypothetical-versus-real moral-decision caveat, and the informal parameter-halving argument. The need for user validation remains.

D1.justification: A new Reproducibility Statement provides a GitHub source-code address and directs readers to methodological details. Appendix B's preprocessing, optimization settings, baseline implementations, hardware, and dataset-license information remain substantively unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds classical-choice and heuristic references, including von Neumann–Morgenstern and additional Tversky works, plus Carnal–Dozzi and Ewerhart–Serena on noise decomposition. It removes the Rosenfeld comparison and citations supporting deleted limitations. These are limited positioning changes; publication-metadata updates for retained works are not new citations.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related-work discussion, theoretical explanations, and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting and condensation. Related Work becomes a separate numbered section, terminology is streamlined, and acknowledgments and a reproducibility statement are added. The editorial revision is broad despite stable experiments.

P2.justification: V2 adopts the ICLR template, revises captions and table labels, moves Figure 2 ahead of the empirical section, and groups Figures 5–8 on one appendix page. All nine figures and Table 1 remain; the underlying graphical content is unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 improves theoretical precision by aligning the factorization theorem's assumptions with its proof, and the new code address improves reproducibility information. These are limited gains with unchanged empirical evidence. They are tempered by removal of the hypothetical-versus-real-decision limitation and the absence of an explicit proof for the added GAM-tree item.
